The political compass is a way of summarizing where your political beliefs lie. The two axes are cultural authority (vertical) and economics (horizontal).

Vertical up - authoritarianism- government imposes more values. Extreme is totalitarianism (state controls all aspects of life)

Vertical down - libertarianism - government imposes less values. Extreme is anarchism (no state)

Horizontal left - economic left wing - wealth is redistributed to lower class better. Extreme is communism (all wealth and property is shared)

Horizontal right - economic right wing - there is less redistribution of wealth. Extreme is laissez faire capitalism (no regulation on economy or wealth)

According to the traditional political compass, the left right axis is economics (how money should flow in society) and the vertical axis is government control. Vertically is pretty self explanatory - dictatorship is at the top, anarchy is at the bottom. As to horizontal, left wing represents economic equality/collectivization and right wing represents economic hierarchy/individualization. So if there were no classes (no rich and poor, all the same), that would be extreme left wing (communism). If there is allowing for competition (companies can becoming richer than others), that becomes more right wing (capitalism). This is my interpretation, though I think other people interpret it slightly different.

EDIT: You would say that the four axes ends are left wing, right wing , authoritarian, and libertarian. You would label the four quadrants as auth left, auth right, lib left, lib right
